findings.claim: ADR-0009 §4-§5 makes `ctx_resume(seq:N)` a required call: an over-640B journal item becomes a pointer line `#<seq> (<bytes> B) ctx_resume(seq:<seq>)`, and the model must call it with a `seq` argument to read the full item. Neither the PRD's tool schema nor the drafts.md tool description mention a `seq` parameter at all, so the model has no documented way to know this call is legal or how to make it.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md:75-76 'It becomes a pointer line: `#<seq> (<bytes> B) ctx_resume(seq:<seq>)`. `ctx_resume(seq:N)` is a primary-key read of the whole row'; PRD-v2.md:128 '**ctx_resume** `{session?}` — ≤ 2 KB summary ... pointers for `ctx_search`' (no `seq` key, and says pointers go to ctx_search, not to ctx_resume itself); docs/v2/prompt/drafts.md:42-47 ctx_resume text: 'Returns a summary of up to 2 KB for this session ... Use it after the conversation was compacted or resumed, before you repeat earlier work.' — never names `seq`. Git archaeology: `seq` has no v1 history (git log -S'ctx_resume' in cm-main shows only session-scoped resume commits f9710b5, c3d04679, 46f3d74 — none pass a sequence number), so this is a new v2 contract that the docs never finished wiring together.
findings.fix: Add `seq?` to the ctx_resume schema in PRD §7 and to the drafts.md ctx_resume description (e.g. 'Pass `seq` from a pointer line in the resume block to read that item in full'), and change PRD-v2.md:128's claim that pointers go to ctx_search so it matches ADR-0009's actual pointer target (ctx_resume, not ctx_search).

findings.claim: `ctx_route` — the tool name ADR-0008/tickets/round4-evidence.json say the Claude Code mcp_tool PreToolUse hook calls (`server:'context-mode', tool:'ctx_route'`) — is still in no tool list, has no drafts.md entry, and ADR-0007's 'tools/list returns the 9 tools' does not name it. DECISIONS-r3.md's Q1-Q19 never settles whether it is listed or hidden. This is the same gap flagged in out/r2/round1/review/prompt.json:12, still open in the r4 docs with no doc change.
findings.evidence: tickets/round4-evidence.json:647 'the hook called ctx_route on the stub server, and the decision took 1.26 ms'; tickets/round4-evidence.json:670 '{type:"mcp_tool", server:"context-mode", tool:"ctx_route", ...}'; grep -rn ctx_route docs/v2/adr/*.md docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md docs/v2/README.md → no hits; docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-spec-2026.md 'tools/list returns the 9 tools in a fixed order' (9 named tools elsewhere are ctx_execute/batch/index/search/resume/stats/doctor/upgrade/purge — ctx_route is not one of them).
findings.fix: Decide in ADR-0007 or ADR-0008 whether ctx_route is a 10th listed tool (needs a drafts.md entry, a budget line, and PR11/PR12 lint coverage) or a hidden/internal-only tool the model never sees in tools/list; state the choice once and update TECH-SPEC §3 and ADR-0007's '9 tools' line to match.

findings.claim: The deny message template (tickets/round4-evidence.json step 5: 'context-mode: predicted ~{b} B ({src}: n={n}, p90={p90} | prior {class} | stat), budget 16384. Run the same command here; the full output is indexed...') never states that a curl/wget/network call was the reason for the deny, even though ADR-0008's own curl/wget rows are a distinct, named deny path. A model seeing only the generic size-prediction message for a denied `curl` call has no textual cue that the network/body-to-stdout rule (not just size) is why it was denied, which matters because the alternative text is the same ctx_execute rewrite either way but the two deny reasons (size vs. body-to-stdout) have different root causes per ADR-0008's own table.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md:11 'curl/wget whose body goes to stdout | ... | deny' and :26 'Deny only when the body reaches stdout' are a separate decision path from the size-based DENY in decideBash; tickets/round4-evidence.json 'DENY MESSAGE' block only ever renders `{src}` as a byte-prediction source (n, p90, prior, stat) with no case for 'network body reaches stdout' as the cited reason.
findings.fix: Either show the message is reused unchanged for both cases (state that explicitly in ADR-0008, since {src} class can already be 'net') or add a short reason clause distinguishing a size deny from a stdout-body-reaches-tool deny.
